summary: All stage-specific semantic checks passed. The BADGE method computes hallucinated final-layer gradient embeddings on the live select_batch path and uses incremental k-MEANS++ distances; the annotated equations are structurally faithful to the paper.

checks_summary.note: kmeans_plus_plus_seeding maintains a running nearest-center squared-distance vector and samples proportionally to it without an all-centers broadcast.
The softmax residual p_i - I(y_hat=i) is multiplied elementwise by the penultimate embedding for every class block, matching Eq. 1.
The implementation uses softmax probabilities and argmax hallucinated labels to form the equivalent cross-entropy gradient expression required by the paper.
Every eq-* paper-element annotation in method.py resolves to an equation element in paper_map.json.

caveats: The zero-distance/equidistant k-MEANS++ fallback samples an unselected point because the paper's probability distribution is undefined when the distance sum is zero; this is a documented edge-case handling choice, not a mismatch at nondegenerate paper scale.
